assessment: Screened out after checking locus geometry: each option repeats its own road, and coloring just a wrong rounded valley would mainly select a locus. There is no corresponding original rounded feature at a sharp road valley to bind without inventing new path ink. Native fragmentation is not itself the reason to reject.
primary_math: On straight slopes the center follows parallel offsets. At convex peaks it traces radius-r arcs; at concave valleys the offset segments meet in a sharp V where support switches. Only E combines rounded peaks and sharp valleys.
